column1: Damage{{efn|All damage totals are in 2016 [[United States dollars|USD]] unless otherwise stated.|group=note|name=Damage}}

column2: Members of the public recorded a brief tornado.
column3: Small tree limbs were broken by this brief tornado.
column4: Trees were snapped or uprooted and a power pole was broken at its rotten base by this large cone tornado.
column5: This large rain-wrapped tornado occurred to the west of Big Spring. A well-constructed home had its roof completely destroyed and multiple exterior walls collapsed, and two other homes had large sections of their roofs removed. An oil pumpjack was overturned, a car was thrown {{convert|100|yd|m|}}, and another car was moved several feet. Two poles were bent, wooden power poles were snapped, and a small barn suffered major loss of roof panels. Trees were damaged along the path as well, with trees partially debarked, trunks snapped, and trees uprooted.
column6: A brief landspout tornado touched down in an open field, causing no damage.
column7: A pivot irrigation system was damaged.
column8: This large but intermittent multiple-vortex tornado passed near the rural community of Plaska, snapping numerous trees and power poles. Several pivot irrigation systems were flipped as well.
column9: An anticyclonic tornado associated with the Big Spring EF3 tornado remained over open fields, causing no damage.
column10: A barn was destroyed, and power lines and two large sections of pivot irrigation were damaged by this large multiple-vortex wedge tornado.
column11: Trees were snapped, power lines were damaged, and pivot irrigation systems were flipped.
column12: Tornado moved along an unusual northwesterly path, producing little damage.
column13: Tree limbs were snapped, a power pole was damaged, and debris was scattered in a field.
column14: Tornado remained over open country, causing no damage.
column15: Eight to ten power poles were snapped and several large trees were heavily damaged.
column16: Tornado formed after the previous Kearny County tornado dissipated, producing no damage as it moved along a northwesterly path over open fields.
column17: A house sustained roof and siding damage, a pole shed was destroyed, several livestock trailers were blown several yards, and a few trees were downed.
column18: A brief tornado touched down over open country, causing no damage.
column19: A rain-wrapped cone tornado remained over open grassland, causing no damage.
column20: 14 power poles were snapped about {{convert|5|ft|m|}} above the ground and a metal building sustained a loss of roof panels.
column21: Large wedge tornado moved along an erratic path through open fields, causing little damage. The tornado was likely capable of producing EF3 or stronger damage based on video evidence.
column22: A large 640 model oil pumpjack was overturned, indicative of EF3 strength winds. Tree branches were broken along other sections of the path.
column23: A tornado moved over open grassland, producing no observable damage.
column24: A single-wide mobile home was rolled and destroyed, another mobile home sustained roof damage, and an oil pumpjack was overturned. A metal barn had its roof purlins buckled and trees had their trunks snapped as well.
column25: A pivot irrigation sprinkler was damaged by the tornado.
column26: Short-lived tornado remained over open country, causing no damage.
column27: Brief tornado remained over open fields, causing no damage.
